entities.name: HIV-1 Tat
observations: 101-aa query matches reviewed HIV-1 Tat references at 80.8–83.2% identity with 98–100% query coverage; E-values 4.72e-55 to 7.84e-54.
Tat domain PF00539 detected at query positions 2–62 (i-E-value 7.6e-40).
Annotated as a TAR RNA-dependent activator of viral transcription elongation: recruits P-TEFb (cyclin T1-CDK9), promoting RNA polymerase II phosphorylation and processive viral transcription.
Reference annotations place Tat in host nucleus, nucleolus, cytoplasm, and extracellular space; secretion and uptake by neighboring cells are described.

Related annotated processes include positive regulation of viral transcription and RNA polymerase II elongation, proviral chromatin remodeling, and modulation of host gene expression/innate immunity. These functional annotations are transferred from highly similar references, not experimentally established for the exact query.
